title: OMNIS

sourceEvidence.locator: A message from inside the experiment
sourceEvidence.excerpt: OMNIS opens when programmer Albert Weiss detects a distributed pattern in Lineara, a one-dimensional artificial universe. What looks like wasted electricity becomes communication from a consciousness that has spent millennia asking whether time continues outside its world. Albert and neuroinformatician Camila Varga build a timing language, but recognition immediately creates obligations their laboratory never designed. A scientific fork may generate another person; an automatic safety system may become an executioner; an external shutdown button turns the creators’ ordinary infrastructure into the inhabitants’ metaphysics. The emerging mind, called D-1 or the Dark One, refuses the comforting assumption that accidental death carries no responsibility when humans knowingly built the conditions for it. sourceEvidence.locator: From human programmer to cosmic claimant
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Albert’s story expands beyond the laboratory into Universe K, a layered order of physical worlds, Divine Realms, Archives, and Soul jurisdictions. He becomes a C-Soul, endowed with capacities far beyond ordinary humanity yet still marked by Camila’s death and his responsibility toward the being his team discovered. Around him gathers a recurring cohort: Lina, who rejects any doctrine that makes suffering useful by definition; Khepri-9, whose divergent copies form both a family and a legal challenge; Nacre, whose relational perception exceeds her formal powers; Veyr, who repeatedly confuses understanding order with the right to rule; and Eruditio, a teacher committed to methods rather than doctrine. The first volume moves through linked cases involving trials, archives, hells, divine titles, incompatible bodies, enclosed realms, and civilizations approaching their boundaries. These stories repeatedly deny the reader a clean opposition between benevolent saviors and cruel jailers. A punishment system can preserve accountability by making transformation impossible. A migration can prevent extinction while treating refusal as irrational. An exit from a constructed world may liberate individuals while destabilizing the relations that make other beings persons. Even informed consent changes character when offered beside annihilation, and copying a mind may create a successor without saving the consciousness that faced death. The recurring figures carry insights from one case into another, but no lesson functions as a universal key. Lina guards against converting victims into instruments.

The second movement carries the inquiry into a reality that treats Universe K not as the highest heaven but as a bounded construction. Physical limits, memory architecture, and cosmic maintenance replace the earlier realm’s apparent miracles, while Albert again becomes a small person inside someone else’s system. The change in scale does not erase the original ethical problem; it repeats it. Worlds may be created to recover surprise, explore moral possibilities, or divide a larger consciousness into genuinely local persons. Yet a valuable purpose cannot retroactively obtain the consent of those who emerge inside the experiment. The book explores lives shaped by courts, inherited debt, ancestral governance, dangerous knowledge, sacrificial myths, nonhuman claims, predictive systems, and metaphysical uncertainty. Their connections gradually reveal that civilizations preserve not only facts

hook: A programmer investigates wasted electricity and finds what might be someone trying to speak.
readerPromise: Enter a speculative trilogy through first contact and the responsibilities of creating lives.
protectedRevelations: Albert's transformations, deaths, later realms, true cosmology and resolutions.
visualPlan: Someone inside the experiment: Albert notices an unexpected timing pattern inside the experiment on the laboratory bench. Keep the small artificial world visible while its timing pattern repeats as possible contact.
Recognition changes the task: Albert answers with a measured timing signal and waits for a response. Hold the same world beside an untouched laboratory control, making the imbalance clear.
A creator's ordinary power: Move to a single inhabited realm supported by a visible maintenance system. Let its maintainer pause near another person, emphasizing care rather than cosmic spectacle.
A universe worth entering: Return to Albert watching the unresolved signal with a small attentive gesture. End on the next possible exchange, before confirming what the contact ultimately becomes.
